highlights:
## Clearer app connection errors

If an app connection cannot start, Nod now shows the connection service's status and a recognized reason. That makes a rate limit or temporary service error easier to distinguish from a sign-in problem when you send feedback.

If an Attio request receives a Cloudflare HTML 403 response, the error includes the UTC time and a validated Ray ID when one is available. Send those details with your feedback so we can trace the request. This adds a diagnostic; it does not change the access rule.

## Quieter background checks

Nod skips connection watch checks for disabled or replaced scheduled jobs. Gmail inbox checks wait until their next scheduled poll after a known connection-service 429 or 503 refusal, instead of retrying immediately. The inbox cursor and completed messages are preserved for the next poll.
